document.title: Pushing for Peace in Afghanistan
document.authors: Karl F. Inderfurth, Assistant Secretary of State for South Asian Affairs, to Secretary of State Albright
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan: "The Taliban's Godfather"?
document.note: [Secret] Fighting will continue as Pakistan supports a Taliban military victory while Iran and Russia back Massoud. Pakistan has not been responsive to requests to use its influence on the Taliban to surrender bin Laden. The U.S. may have to treat the Taliban as an intrinsic enemy and pariah state.

key_claims: The US assumed Pakistan would continue to seek and support a Taliban military victory.
Pakistan has not been responsive to US requests to press the Taliban to surrender Bin Ladin and could do more, including cutting POL supplies flowing from Pakistan.
The US proposed shifting from Six Plus Two to an 'Eight Minus One' format to isolate Pakistan if diplomacy fails.
The US contemplated seeking Security Council backing, including Chapter Seven reference, to enforce cessation of outside support to Afghan factions.
Iran and Russia provide covert military support to Masood but are likelier to end it than Pakistan is to end Taliban support.
The Taliban has become the vehicle of Pushtun ethnic power and may be considered an intrinsic enemy of the US.
Recognition of the Taliban could be considered only if it removes Bin Ladin and terror networks, acts against narcotics, and improves human rights.
